common-senses.title: Common SENSES
common-senses.subtitle: Research Assistant / Boston Area Research Initiative
common-senses.intro: I analyze Boston PM2.5 sensor readings in Python and R for BARI and Boston’s Office of Emerging Technology. I compare locations and months, check missing data and make maps.

body.text:
DATA AND PREPARATION
My September 2026 source contains 1,030,999 air-quality measurements across 24 locations. I convert timestamps to Boston local time, reconcile sensor deployments with physical locations and consolidate duplicate location-minute observations.

QUALITY AND COVERAGE
I test working completeness rules, including 45 valid minutes for an hourly average and 18 valid hours for a daily average. Coverage assumptions remain subject to team review. Missing historical records and incomplete month-end coverage are tracked rather than treated as zero pollution.

MATCHED HISTORICAL COMPARISON
I compare the same 12 locations across September 2025, August 2026 and September 2026, giving each site equal weight. The matched averages were 5.15, 6.37 and 3.59 µg/m³ respectively; all 12 locations had lower September 2026 averages than in both comparison months.

TIME-OF-DAY ANALYSIS
I prepare overnight, morning, midday and evening maps, an evening-minus-midday comparison and variation-between-days figures. The time-of-day maps use arithmetic averages at 24 locations over the same 25 September dates. Hourly profiles instead use medians and interquartile bands; I keep those summaries distinct.

REPRODUCIBLE OUTPUTS
The project includes 24 published figures, aggregate tables, runnable R scripts and R Markdown reports. The workflow rebuilds figures from checked local inputs and keeps source provenance, analysis settings and output runs separate.

INTERPRETATION
The maps describe sensor-point measurements, rather than neighborhood-wide exposure. Boston Logan weather is contextual information. These comparisons do not establish which sources or interventions caused a change.

MAP CREDIT
The study-boundary print shown here is adapted from Tasnim’s R map source using the supplied boundary. It is not presented as my original cartographic work.

tbca.title: TBCA
tbca.subtitle: Foundations of Data Science / Northeastern
tbca.intro: I built two employment regressions and a funding-allocation model using Eurostat data from 27 EU countries. I wrote the prediction functions and added them to our Flask, MySQL and Streamlit app.

body.text:
DATA ENGINEERING
I pulled Eurostat employment by NACE sector (nama_10_a64_e) and tertiary graduates by ISCED field (educ_uoe_grad02), covering 27 EU countries from 2012 to 2023. I hand-built the ISCED–NACE crosswalk and merged the sources into a panel of approximately 2,354 rows across eight sectors.

FEATURES
I created lagged employment and year-over-year change variables, then standardized the model inputs with StandardScaler. The crosswalk made the graduate classifications usable alongside sector-level employment records.

TWO EMPLOYMENT MODELS
Model 1 predicts employment level from the prior year’s employment. Model 2 predicts year-over-year employment change from year, graduate count and lagged employment.




TEMPORAL VALIDATION
I replaced the random train/test split with training years 2012–2020 and holdout years 2021–2023. I recognized that the level model’s near-perfect R² was dominated by persistence in employment, rather than proof of strong forward prediction. The revised change model reached approximately R² = 0.21.

FROM NOTEBOOK TO APPLICATION
I stored coefficients, intercepts and scaler parameters in MySQL tables model1_params and model2_params. I wrote DB-backed prediction functions in labor.py and a retraining pipeline in train.py, then built a Streamlit labor dashboard with Plotly charts and a prediction widget populated from the selected country and sector.

FUNDING-ALLOCATION MODEL
In budget.py, I combined a per-sector OLS employment trend, graduate absorption and the employment outlook into standardized demand signals. Softmax converts those signals to target budget shares, which are blended with existing allocations to produce recommendations.

INTEGRATION
I connected model outputs through Flask routes and MySQL, added budget-plan navigation and debugged database cursor and route-registration issues. The team’s Streamlit frontend communicates with the Flask REST API; the API reads and writes MySQL.

BOUNDARIES OF MY CONTRIBUTION
I owned the labor models and budget-model work described above. The university recommendation model, broader database design and other persona interfaces were shared team contributions. The funding outputs are recommendations, not government allocation decisions.

peak.title: PEAK research
peak.subtitle: Computational Researcher / PEAK Summit Fellowship
peak.intro: I write Python simulations to compare Texas and North Carolina congressional maps with alternative district plans. I check the source data and test whether the Markov chains have sampled reliably.

body.text:
CONVERGENCE
I evaluate rank-based R-hat and bulk and tail effective sample size for multiple metrics. Starting-map groups and dispersed-start cohorts are checked separately and jointly. Checkpoints and continued-run audits keep diagnostics tied to the exact chains being interpreted.

RESEARCH QUESTION
How unusual are enacted districting plans relative to alternative plans sampled under stated population and contiguity constraints? This is PEAK Award research at Northeastern, advised by Dr. Eric Gerber.

SOURCE AND GEOGRAPHY
I match Census population, Redistricting Data Hub election allocations and official plan assignments by block ID. I check coverage, totals, geometry, adjacency and contiguity before analyzing a plan.



RECOM SAMPLING
I run independent GerryChain ReCom Markov chains, preserving primary population bounds of ±0.1% in Texas and ±0.5% in North Carolina. Texas has 38 districts; the baseline uses 9,712 geographic units. North Carolina’s common geography retains 236,638 Census blocks within 2,681 units.

CURRENT RESEARCH STATUS
The repository records a frozen North Carolina baseline at 23,000 states per chain, with six chains and both starting-map groups passing the primary screens. Texas continuation and dispersed-start checks are kept separate; I do not present its earlier audit as a fully converged final result.

COMPARISONS
I compare enacted maps with ensemble distributions of seat and geographic measures, and keep election-model, constraint and geography sensitivities as separate experiments. Earlier Texas demos and reports are preserved as historical work rather than mixed into the rebuilt baseline.

LIMITATIONS
Votes are modeled allocations of presidential election results. The implemented ReCom process is not a claim of uniform sampling or full legal compliance. Tail frequencies are descriptive, and low-frequency results require adequate sampling diagnostics.

REPRODUCIBILITY
The repository documents pinned dependencies, source validation, state-level commands, checkpoint continuation, freeze rules and generated paper tables and figures.

forge.title: Forge
forge.subtitle: Software Product Lab Member / Northeastern
forge.intro: I design screens in Figma and build account, profile, student-verification and listing features for Husky Marketplace. I also test sign-in and onboarding with the team.

body.text:
ACCOUNT AND DEVICE VERIFICATION
I built the account-setup flow from email verification through profile completion to Home. Profiles include a unique username, campus, school year, optional bio and photo. Username checks use the existing lower(username) database index.

I also worked on remembered-browser and new-device behavior: requesting and resending codes, preserving a pending code after refresh, correcting the countdown when switching tabs, and allowing temporary errors to retry without signing the user out.

HOME LISTINGS
I connected Home to the four newest approved, available listings. The screen has separate loading, empty, error and retry states. A failed live request does not silently fall back to demo listings.

PROFILE PHOTOS
I implemented photo upload, saved-photo reload, replacement and removal, including updates to the header avatar. I reused a teammate’s compression helper and tested recovery from a failed upload.

The proposed Storage policy uses a private WebP-only bucket, a 256 KB limit, owner-only writes and verified-student reads through signed URLs. That migration is awaiting review and is not installed on shared Supabase.

VALIDATION
PR #52 records 89 passing frontend tests, 111 database assertions and 27 browser checks against a local production build and local Supabase. The checks cover signup, account setup, photo changes, incorrect codes, refresh, remembered and mobile browsers, invalid device cookies and password recovery.

The checks also include deliberate 503 responses for an upload and a device request to test recovery. TypeScript, linting, formatting and the production build pass for the branch.

DESIGN AND RELEASE STATUS
I designed mobile and desktop flows in Figma and kept the product’s existing Archivo and DM Sans typefaces during implementation. The PR includes screenshots for review.

These changes are still in review and require combined testing with the team’s other account work. Hosted signup, reset, new-device and photo checks remain part of release validation. Messaging is a later feature.

accounting.title: Managerial Accounting
accounting.subtitle: ACCT 2301 / Profit Analysis for Managers and Advisors
accounting.intro: I use Excel to model how costs, volume and sales mix affect operating profit. The course also develops overhead-allocation and relevant-cost analysis for comparing business alternatives.

body.text:
COST-VOLUME-PROFIT ANALYSIS
I build linked Excel models for sales, variable costs, contribution margin, fixed costs and operating income. I compare break-even points, target profit and changes in sales mix using formulas and data tables.

SCENARIO DESIGN
Inputs and calculated outputs are connected rather than entered as independent answers. I examine how changing price, unit volume or costs affects the result, including the assumptions behind each comparison.

COST TRACING AND ALLOCATION
Coursework distinguishes direct from indirect costs, cost pools and appropriate cost drivers. I work with predetermined overhead rates, allocated overhead, unit manufacturing cost, cost of goods sold and ending inventory.




ACTIVITY-BASED COSTING
I compare traditional allocation with multiple ABC activity pools, distinguishing unit-, batch-, product- and facility-level activities. The analysis examines how cost-driver choice changes apparent product costs.

RELEVANT-COST DECISIONS
I separate future differential costs from sunk and unavoidable costs when studying special orders, make-or-buy choices and equipment replacement. Opportunity costs, avoidable fixed costs and capacity conditions matter to the recommendation.

RELATED COMPLETED COURSE
ACCT 1201 / Financial Accounting and Reporting introduced the statements and accounting information used to understand business performance. ACCT 2301 builds on that foundation with managerial analysis.

statistics.title: Business Statistics
statistics.subtitle: MGSC 2301 / Business Statistics
statistics.intro: I analyze eBay auction data to examine opening prices and bidder participation. I use Python and Excel for data preparation, descriptive statistics, visualization and correlation analysis.

body.text:
DATA AND QUESTION
The eBay analysis starts with 1,953 Cartier bid records summarized into 136 auctions. I examine the relationship between the opening bid and the number of bids rather than treating every bid record as a separate auction.

DATA PREPARATION
I use Python/pandas and Excel to organize the records and create auction-level summaries. Counts and opening bids must be checked at the auction level before calculating statistics.

DISTRIBUTION SUMMARIES
For both variables, the work includes count, mean, median, mode, minimum, maximum, range, variance, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, quartiles, IQR and the five-number summary. Skewness and kurtosis describe distribution shape.




EXCEL METHODS
I use the Data Analysis ToolPak and formulas including QUARTILE.EXC, STDEV.S, VAR.S, MODE.SNGL and COVARIANCE.S. I construct IQR fences at Q1 − 1.5 × IQR and Q3 + 1.5 × IQR to identify potential outliers.

VISUALIZATION
Histograms show the distributions and their skew; boxplots show quartiles, spread and flagged observations. I check histogram bins rather than relying on an automatic choice that can hide most auctions inside one interval.

ASSOCIATION
The analysis reports a correlation of approximately −0.32 between opening bid and bid count. This describes association in the observed sample, not a causal estimate of how changing a seller’s price will affect participation.

REPORTING AND CHECKS
I reconcile the auction counts, summary statistics, outlier flags and charts, then explain the results in a written report. Live formulas, consistent quartile conventions and the treatment of real high-value auctions matter to reproducibility.
